cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: Limelit launches agentic GEO platform with MCP server and 211 automation tools
stories.plain: Limelit connects Claude, ChatGPT, and other AI assistants to a platform that tracks brand visibility inside six AI search engines and runs autonomous GEO workflows. Agents identify content gaps and produce governed, approved content to close them. This matters because it turns GEO from a manual audit task into a self-operating system any marketing team can run.

stories.head: EngageLab's Agent Email lets AI agents receive, understand, and reply to customer emails at scale
stories.plain: Aurora Mobile's EngageLab moves AI beyond outbound sends: its Agent Email infrastructure lets AI agents read inbound replies, answer them using a private knowledge base, and write intent signals back into CRM. Replies stay threaded in Gmail and Outlook. This shifts email from a broadcast tool to a two-way agentic channel, changing how engagement platforms are built.

stories.head: Peec AI launches Peec Agent to help marketing teams act on AI search brand signals
stories.plain: Peec Agent, used by 3,500+ companies, now delivers evidence-backed recommendations across technical, content, and third-party opportunities and can execute actions — not just report findings. It closes the loop between monitoring what AI search engines say about a brand and actually changing that representation, making GEO an active rather than passive discipline.

stories.head: Personalization works best when it targets what customers want, not who they are
stories.plain: This piece argues that intent-based personalization outperforms identity-based profiling: consumers value useful, relevant offers but will leave if brands demand personal data without a clear benefit. It reframes the data-collection debate — less 'who are you?' and more 'what do you need right now?' — with direct implications for how CDPs and personalization engines should be designed.

stories.head: ThoughtSpot's AgentSpot prices AI analytics by business outcome, not seat
stories.plain: AgentSpot positions itself as a multiplayer AI workforce grounded in company data, moving beyond single-user chatbots. ThoughtSpot's outcome-based pricing model — paying for results rather than licenses — signals a new commercial pattern for enterprise AI that could reshape how marketing AI tools are bought and budgeted across teams.

stories.head: Salesforce's $5.7B Braze acquisition reshapes the customer engagement platform market
stories.plain: Salesforce is acquiring Braze, a leading customer engagement platform, for $5.7 billion. This is a major consolidation move that changes the competitive landscape for how brands buy and operate marketing technology. Any team evaluating CEP vendors or Salesforce's Data Cloud ecosystem now has a materially different set of options and lock-in risks to consider.

stories.head: Aurora Mobile's EngageLab launches Agent Email: AI agents that receive and reply to customer email at scale
stories.plain: EngageLab's Agent Email lets AI agents handle inbound customer replies — reading, understanding, and responding — while staying threaded in Gmail and Outlook and writing intent signals back to CRM. This moves AI email from just sending to fully autonomous two-way conversation, a significant shift in how customer engagement pipelines are built and governed.

stories.head: Limelit launches agentic GEO platform with MCP server giving AI agents 211 tools to automate AI search visibility
stories.plain: Limelit's platform connects Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor to a generative engine optimization workflow that tracks brand visibility across six AI search engines and runs governed agents to turn visibility gaps into approved content automatically. It signals how GEO is maturing from monitoring into autonomous action, changing how marketing teams staff and budget for AI search.

stories.head: Peec AI launches Peec Agent to let marketing teams act on what AI search engines say about their brand
stories.plain: Peec Agent, used by over 3,500 companies, now goes beyond reporting to give evidence-backed recommendations and autonomous actions on how brands appear in AI search results. This shifts GEO from a reporting discipline into an agentic workflow, meaning marketers need to think about governance guardrails alongside visibility strategy.

stories.head: ChatGPT sends less than 1% of Google's traffic but converts at a higher rate
stories.plain: New data shows ChatGPT drives under 1% of Google's traffic volume, yet those visitors convert at a higher rate — while Google organic still produces 27 times more total conversions than all LLMs combined. This benchmark gives marketers a concrete basis for deciding how much budget to shift toward GEO versus traditional SEO right now.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Take Over the Full Marketing Workflow
body: The past month marks a clear inflection point: AI is no longer just generating content or scoring leads — it is executing end-to-end marketing tasks autonomously. EngageLab's Agent Email receives and answers customer replies without human intervention; Limelit deploys 211 tools to automate GEO workflows; AgentSpot moves from single chatbots to coordinated multi-agent systems.

This shift from assistants to autonomous operators forces a structural question: who owns the decisions AI agents are making, and what data do they act on? Building a reliable source of truth — clean, governed, accessible — is now a prerequisite, not a nice-to-have, for any team deploying agentic martech.
ev: MarTech · Agents need a source of truth

themes.head: MCP Becomes the New Integration Standard for MarTech
body: Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers are quietly becoming the connective tissue of modern martech stacks. Framer launched an official MCP server so outside AI agents can build and edit websites directly; GeeLark added MCP support to its cloud phone workflows; Limelit built its GEO automation layer on MCP. Multiple independent vendors converging on the same protocol in a single month is a standardization signal, not a coincidence.

For martech buyers, MCP adoption means the composability question is shifting from APIs to agent-readable interfaces. Teams that choose platforms with MCP support today are preserving optionality to plug in whatever AI orchestration layer wins — rather than locking into a single vendor's agent runtime.

themes.head: AI Search Reshapes Brand Discoverability at Its Root
body: AI search engines are transforming how buyers research products — prompts are replacing queries, and the content that surfaces inside an AI answer is becoming the new top-of-funnel. Creator content is already shaping AI product recommendations, and CommerceIQ's CEO frames retail-media and product content as a single discoverability system, not separate channels. Peec AI launched an agent specifically to monitor and act on what AI search says about a brand.

Meanwhile, data showing ChatGPT still sends less than 1% of Google's traffic is a useful corrective: AI search influence on purchase decisions is already large even when referral traffic looks small, because the research happens inside the model. Marketers who wait for traffic dashboards to signal the shift will arrive late.
ev: MarTech · Creator content shapes AI recommendations

themes.head: Personalization Pivots to Intent, Not Identity
body: A maturing signal in this month's coverage is the explicit rejection of identity-based personalization in favor of behavioral intent signals. The argument is practical: knowing what a customer wants in the moment — inferred from context, content consumption, and decision patterns — is more actionable than a demographic profile, and survives privacy constraints that are dismantling third-party identity graphs.

This aligns with the broader shift from customer journeys to real-time decisions described in the 'next era of customer engagement' piece. Marketers are being asked to architect systems that decide, not just segment — which means AI inference engines, not CRM records, become the personalization backbone going forward.
ev: Agile Brand · Measure AI by customers kept

themes.head: Composable Architecture Becomes the Default Stack Decision
body: Composable martech — assembling best-of-breed modules rather than buying a monolithic suite — has crossed from trend to working assumption. The driver is speed of AI change: no single platform can iterate fast enough to cover every emerging AI capability, so teams that locked into suites are already hitting ceilings. Composability is the structural answer to an environment where the tooling changes quarterly.

The practical consequence is that data architecture decisions now precede vendor decisions. CEOs are asking questions dashboards cannot answer, skills gaps cannot be papered over with headcount or AI alone, and AI governance needs the kind of deliberate policy layer email marketing built over decades. Composable stacks only deliver their promise if the underlying data, governance, and skills are solid — making this theme inseparable from every other shift in this month's coverage.

month.takeaway: Every major move this month — agentic automation, MCP standardization, AI-search discoverability, intent-led personalization, and composable stacks — converges on one irreversible reality: the martech stack is being rebuilt around AI inference rather than human workflow, and teams that treat this as a tooling upgrade rather than an architectural rethink will find themselves optimizing a system that no longer matches how customers or markets actually behave.
